subject: Quick follow: prompt data traceability & storage details
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quick follow: prompt data traceability & storage details

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I wanted to summarize where Redwood stands on what we keep, where it lives, and how long it’s retained so your privacy/compliance team has something concise to review. I’ve kept this short and added two quick attachments: a one-page prompt-data matrix and our SOC 2 summary.

High-level recap (answers to the three asks you raised):
- What is stored: by default, Redwood Hosted logs request metadata and aggregated telemetry. Prompt inputs and model outputs are not persisted long-term on hosted products unless the customer opts into storage (e.g., for fine-tuning, analytics, or QA). When opted-in, stored artifacts are: request payloads (prompt text), generated outputs, token-level usage logs (for billing), and trace IDs for routing/debugging.
- Where it’s stored: we store opted-in artifacts in region-specific object stores (e.g., us-east1). Customers can request EU residency (eu-west1) for dedicated/private deployments. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers data remains in your environment.
- How long: default retention for opted-in prompt/output artifacts is 90 days with a configurable TTL down to 7 days or up to 365 days under an enterprise contract. Ephemeral logs (used for live troubleshooting and autoscaling) are retained for 24 hours and then purged.

Controls we discussed:
- Redaction & filtering: you can configure automatic PII redaction rules (regex-based + common PHI detection).
- Customer-managed keys (KMS): available for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports KMS-backed storage for enterprise plans.
- Audit logs & access: full access logs for retrieval requests and operator actions are retained for 1 year and can be exported to your SIEM.
- Disable storage: option to disable persistent prompt/output storage entirely — only token-usage counters and anonymized metrics remain.

Next steps I’ll take: attach the two docs and add Ben (pricing) + Monica (security) on the thread so we can commit to a concrete TTL/residency combo that fits HealthCore’s requirements. Can you confirm whether HealthCore needs EU residency or if US-only is acceptable for the proof-of-concept?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Quick follow: prompt data traceability & storage details

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. A couple clarifying questions from our side before we loop legal: 
1) When a customer opts in to store prompts/outputs, is the stored output exactly the model response text or do you also store intermediate artifacts (attention maps, raw logits, hidden states)?
2) For the 90-day default, is there a hard delete/secure wipe procedure after TTL expires? We need assurance for audits.
3) Is there a simple API toggle we can call to turn storage on/off per environment (staging vs prod)?

Also, HealthCore requires that any persisted PII is encrypted-at-rest with keys we control for production. For the POC we can accept Redwood-managed keys in US, but legal will want KMS for production.

—Sarah
Director of Platform Engineering, HealthCore

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow: prompt data traceability & storage details

Great questions — see answers below. I’ve pasted Monica on the technical bits and Ben on the commercial commitments.

Sarah — answers:
1) Stored artifacts: we only persist request payloads (prompt text) and final model outputs when a customer explicitly opts into prompt/output storage. We do not persist raw model internals (hidden states, attention maps, logits) as part of normal storage for hosted services. Those are ephemeral in the runtime and never written to object storage.

2) Deletion: yes, TTL-driven deletion is enforced. At expiration we perform a secure delete (object store delete + metadata zeroization). For enterprise customers we can run a deletion job that issues S3-style object lifecycle deletes and provide an audit manifest showing object keys removed and timestamps. Monica can add more on verification.

3) API toggle: yes — storage is configurable at the project/environment level via our Management API. Flags are: storage.enabled (boolean), storage.ttl_days (integer), storage.region (string), storage.kms_key (string optional). For POC you can enable storage for a sandbox project and set ttl_days=30. For production you can configure customer-managed KMS and region=us-east1 or eu-west1.

Monica — can you add the short note on access logs and SIEM export?

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah — quick add from security:
- Access logs: retrievals of stored prompts/outputs generate audit events (who, which key, requestor IP, reason). Those audit logs are retained for 12 months by default and can be exported in near-real-time to your SIEM (Splunk/ELK) via a secure forwarder or S3 export.
- Proofs & verification: we can provide an audit manifest after TTL-based purges (list of object keys and timestamps) and a signed statement of deletion on request for enterprise contracts.
- Redaction best practice: we recommend tokenization + client-side hashing of PHI fields on ingestion where possible (we’ll include example scripts).

Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level controls)

—Monica
